quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: The first thing alcohol affects is:

options.text: Vision.
Judgment.
Balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects judgment before other abilities. It enters your stomach, goes into your blood, and spreads to your brain. Alcohol damages the parts of your brain that control judgment and skills needed for safe driving.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires slide on water instead of touching the road. To prevent hydroplaning in rain, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep your speed steady.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder when rain starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: In rainy weather, slow down to avoid hydroplaning. Driving too fast causes your tires to ride up on water and lose grip on the road. This makes your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content and its effects on your body.

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body and stops its harmful effects.

questions.question: When a school bus stops on the road to load or unload children, you must:

options.text: Stop completely until all children leave the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is raised.
Change lanes and pass the bus slowly and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is raised.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and a stop arm out, you must stop completely. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the arm is raised before you move. Even after the bus moves, wait to make sure no children are crossing the road.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you have the right-of-way. Look at the situation at each intersection. Give up your right-of-way if it helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: You should not stop suddenly in front of large trucks and buses because:

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more time and distance to stop than small cars. A sudden stop in front of a large vehicle may cause a crash because the driver cannot stop in time.

questions.question: Which of these is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam lights in fog.
Staring only at the road ahead.
Checking your rearview mirrors often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every 2 to 5 seconds to see hazards around you. Do not stare only ahead—this is unsafe. In fog, use low beams, not high beams.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the center of a road mean passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either side.

questions.question: If you need your lights on while driving due to weather or poor light:

options.text: Use parking lights.
Use high beams.
Use low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect light back at you, causing glare and making it harder to see.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving and taking medicine?

options.text: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medicines do not affect driving if you take the right dose.
Prescription medicines are always safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medicines—prescription or over-the-counter—can affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy. You must know how your medicine affects your ability to drive.

questions.question: When can you legally block an intersection?

options.text: If you entered on a green light.
During rush hour.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can drive completely across before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection is illegal and you can be cited.

questions.question: When should you not use your horn?

options.text: When you cannot see far ahead.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Using your horn near a blind pedestrian can be dangerous. Yield to the pedestrian and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal rapidly several times.
Slow down gradually without braking.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without braking.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Take your foot off the gas and do not brake. Let the vehicle slow on its own. Use brakes gently only if needed. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road ahead.
Do not enter.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has curves.

questions.question: As you drive faster, what is important to do?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: At higher speeds, your vehicle needs more distance to stop. Look well ahead so you have time to react safely to hazards.

questions.question: How do sudden wind gusts on highways affect drivers?

options.text: They only affect large vehicles.
They only reduce visibility.
They can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers. It can reduce visibility by blowing dust and dirt, and it can physically move any vehicle.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Stay farther back than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back than normal.
questions.explanation: Keep a three- to four-second distance behind motorcycles. They can stop quickly. Extra distance protects both of you if the rider falls. Risk of falling is highest on wet roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges and railroad tracks.

questions.question: On a highway with a single broken white line, what can you do?

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may cross only if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross a white dashed line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow to 25 mph before entering the lane.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when clear.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic on the interstate. Then merge smoothly when it is safe. Do not stop.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Use your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Speed up to avoid accidents.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beams. If fog is too thick to see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: A pedestrian is walking on the road and an oncoming vehicle is approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at the same speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to get the pedestrian to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one road hazard at a time. Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of a road mean?

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means any driver can pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does a blood alcohol concentration of 0.02 percent do?

options.text: It has no effect on your driving.
It does not put other drivers at risk.
It doubles your chance of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: It doubles your chance of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Every 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol nearly doubles a driver's risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Continue and clear the intersection safely.
Speed up so you do not cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue and clear the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, clear it as quickly as possible.

questions.question: When must you use your low beams?

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off these conditions and create glare. Some cars have fog lights that should be used with low beams.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
Do not turn left.
Do not make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not turn left.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left. It is unsafe and against the law to turn left where this sign is posted.

questions.question: You see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Construction signs warn you of workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to low gear before going down steep hills.
Stay close to the car ahead to keep traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Shift to low gear before steep hills to prevent skidding. Follow farther behind other vehicles than normal. Avoid quick stops. Pump your brakes if you don't have antilock brakes.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines between lanes mean?

options.text: You can pass from the left.
You can pass from the right.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Directions for children
School zone ahead
Playground area ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone ahead
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that you are in or near a school zone. Watch for children and follow posted speed limits.
